name: 1994 retro (Jim Olsen)
description: Sun Country's 1994 scheme recreated on the 737-800 N826SY: a white fuselage; orange over the lower nose, narrowing aft under the windows; from under the title a red band appears below the orange, a thin white line between them, and behind the wing both sweep up, the orange as a thin stripe to the crown just ahead of the fin, the red widening over the windows to cover the rear fuselage and tail cone; 'Sun Country' in big slanted red letters outlined in white across the forward windows, the 'y' dropping into the orange; the fin red with a white tip and today's sun-and-S logomark in white; white fillet and engines; the registration in red with a small US flag after it.

notes: Measured off Sun Country's own press photo of N826SY's right side (May 2026, flipped nose-left), fitted to shapes/B738.json. The photo is a little from behind with a short lens, and one fit couldn't hold both ends (the nose came out 15-30 px off), so the forward fuselage was read through a fit on the nose, forward door, first window and the crown and belly at 4 and 10 m, the aft fuselage through one on the tail, fin tip, aft door and the crown and belly at 23 and 32 m: positions about 0.01-0.015 of the length either way. The wing and engine hide the stripes from about x 0.34 to 0.52: drawn straight through. The orange over the nose is in shade and its lowest edge near the nose tip is the least sure part. The fin was measured off its own outline in the photo (its edges are the fin space, so the fit's narrower 737 fin didn't matter): the white tip from 0.885 of the height at the leading edge to 0.755 at the trailing edge; the sun-and-S centered at x 0.656, 0.354 up, 0.74 tall to its rays' tips; white at the leading edge's foot behind the white fillet. The leading edge shows a thin white edge (paint or the bare boot, unclear): not drawn. The red band is lit unevenly (bright under the white line, darker at the windows): one red. Titles: the right side shows 'Sun Country' from x 0.093 to 0.409 and it's drawn over the same stretch on the left (the left-side press photos show 'Country' running aft toward the wing, its start hidden by the stairs). Its white outline shows only where the y crosses the orange and isn't drawn. Not drawn: 'BOEING 737-800' small above the aft windows, the Jim Olsen dedication decal by the forward door. The 2026-09-11 Commons photo (right side from ahead) agrees with the press photos but was too foreshortened to fit.

areas.name: orange: broad over the lower nose, narrowing aft under the windows, then a stripe sweeping up behind the wing to the crown ahead of the fin
red: a wedge from under the title, below a thin white line, widening aft over the windows and covering the rear fuselage and tail cone
white tip, its lower edge sagging toward the trailing edge
white at the leading edge's foot, behind the white fillet

logos.description: Today's sun-and-S logomark in white on the red fin: the S in a ring, separate rays round it; the rays reach down to the fin's root and the ring runs a little past the trailing edge.
A small US flag after the registration (on the right side, forward of it).
The flag after the registration on the left side, aft of it: placed as the right side's mirror, no photo shows it.

titles.style: Sun Country's 1994 logotype: big heavy slanted letters, capital S and C, in red outlined in white across the forward windows, sitting on the orange, the y's tail dropping into it.
The aircraft's own registration in red capitals on the white under the red band, ahead of the aft door.
